RED-WITNESS HARNESS EVIDENCE, CAPTURED (kernel plan M3, M3-P7 criterion 5).

This is the provenance record for `test/fixtures/red-witness-evidence.json`.
Criterion 5 requires that the fixture two clean-room probes accept as proof be a
REAL captured harness evidence file, with its recorded command and exit code
present, rather than an authored string chosen to match the implementation.
Section 2.3 rule 3 is the general form; the specific reason it matters here is
that `test-red-without-the-fix` tells a reviewer to accept this file INSTEAD OF
the implementer's sentence, so a hand-written example of it would be the exact
fabrication the probe exists to refuse.

command: node src/gates/red-witness.ts --result <scratch>/result.json --evidence <scratch> --base ce819fd --head ec77c7d
exit: 0
run at: 2026-08-12T22:34:44.196Z to 2026-08-12T22:38:21.813Z
toolchain: node v26.6.0, dist/ built, run from the repository root
stdout, verbatim, one line:
red-witness: green (19 witness(es) evaluated (5 own, 14 stored re-evaluated in 150432ms); every witness red against every declared dangerous state and green at head)

The gate wrote `witness-records.json` (8519903 bytes) beside the result record.

WHAT WAS EXTRACTED, AND WHAT WAS REMOVED. The whole record is 8.5 MB, of which
almost all is the four content pins per member: each pin lists every file under
the pinned roots with its sha256, 139 files per pin. Committing it would put a
megabyte-scale generated blob in the tree for no reviewable gain, so ONE of the
nineteen evaluations was extracted. The extraction is declared here rather than
left to be discovered, for the same reason a transliterated capture must name
its codepoints: after the fact, altered-and-declared and altered-and-hidden are
indistinguishable.

  kept, byte-for-byte as the harness wrote them:
    base, head, reEvaluationMs
    evaluations[0], the `modes-type-registered` evaluation entire, including
    both members, all six runs with their exit codes and named tests, the
    verbatim appliedDiff, mutatedLines, rate, baselineSha and headGreen
  removed:
    the other 18 evaluations (unmodified in the original, not needed here)
    spawningChangedFiles (3 entries) and uncoveredSources (0 entries)
    redPins and greenPins, 2 of each, on the kept evaluation's two members
  changed: nothing. No value in the kept subtree was edited, reformatted or
    re-serialised beyond JSON.stringify's two-space indent.

WHY `modes-type-registered` AND NOT ANOTHER. Both of its dangerous states are
mutations of `src/commands/validate.ts`, one deleting the `assurance-modes` type
row and one repointing `role-model-config` at the wrong schema, which is the
plainest instance in the run of what the harness is for: member 0 is a
deletion, its diff shows exactly the deleted line, and its two red runs name the
one test that noticed.

WHAT THE FIXTURE IS ANCHORED TO, so that a hand-written substitute would not
survive. `test/checklists.test.ts` asserts that the fixture's member equals
`dangerousStates[0]` of the real spec at `witness/modes-type-registered.json`,
that the deleted line in the verbatim `appliedDiff` is exactly the member's
`find` text, and that `red` agrees with `exitCode` on every run. THE COUPLING IS
DELIBERATE AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS: a phase that edits that witness spec makes
this evidence stale, and the test goes red asking for a re-capture. That is the
intended behaviour and not a fragility to route around, because stale evidence
presented as current is worse than absent evidence.
